title: cadintent civil pack v0
description: The civil pack's v0 schema: sanitary and storm gravity networks. Node kinds manhole / catch_basin / outfall / structure, one edge kind (conduit), and the network object. Facts land through the core object.* commands as typed attrs; only kind, geometry, and (for edges) end bindings are required at creation — missing expected facts are completeness findings, never refusals. Inverts live solely on conduit ends (a/b); structures never store them. Slope and length are never stored — always derived. Spec version 0.1.0.

NetworkSystem.description: The system a network serves — closed because the charter scope is exactly these two and every pack check keys off it. Combined/diversion situations are multi-membership, never a 'combined' value.

FlowDirection.description: The declared per-conduit flow-direction fact: from end_a to end_b, or the reverse. Never part of core topology; a pack check re-derives direction from end inverts and flags disagreement, flat, or adverse grades as findings carrying both values.

ConduitShapeName.description: The closed conduit shape enum — closed because shape dictates which size facts are meaningful: 'circular' expects attrs.diameter; 'box' and 'arch' expect attrs.span and attrs.rise.

CircularShape.description: The assembled shape+size view of a circular conduit. Sizes are SI quantized decimal strings (a 250 mm pipe is '0.250').

ConduitShape.description: One conduit shape with its per-shape size fields, assembled from the conduit's shape/size attrs.

Material.description: A pipe or structure material — an open non-empty string paired with the pack's versioned material vocabulary (x-cadintent-pack). The vocabulary check flags off-list values as findings, never refusals: municipalities differ, and the schema does not pretend to own that list.

ManholeFacts.description: The optional domain facts of a manhole (all added by later commands as the design is learned; only kind and location are required at creation). rim_elevation is the lid; sump_elevation the inside bottom. Connecting-pipe inverts are per-conduit-end facts — this schema deliberately has no slot for them.

CatchBasinFacts.description: Same field set as a manhole; rim_elevation is the grate. A catch basin's lead is an ordinary conduit, not a field.

OutfallFacts.description: An outfall (covers headwalls). No rim — an outfall's elevations live on the conduit end that binds to it.

receiving.description: Free text: what the outfall discharges to.

StructureFacts.description: The generic structure escape hatch: the manhole field set plus a free-text description so intent isn't lost.

ConduitFacts.description: One edge kind for both systems — which system a conduit serves is its network membership, not its type. Inverts are per-end facts keyed a/b; slope and length are never stored (derived from end inverts and plan geometry — design-intent slope enters as basis on the command writing the inverts).

NetworkFacts.description: A complete network carries exactly one domain fact: the system it serves. Missing at creation is a completeness finding, never a refusal.
